title: It's time to pass the CLARITY Act - a16z crypto
gist: a16z's Chris Dixon argues the GENIUS Act already proved regulatory clarity accelerates stablecoin growth and capital formation, and calls for the CLARITY Act to extend the same framework to the 85% of the crypto market (blockchain networks) that remains unregulated, warning the U.S. risks ceding financial-infrastructure leadership if it doesn't act.

themes.theme: GENIUS Act as proof that regulatory clarity accelerates growth

insights.claim: The GENIUS Act's reserve requirements and issuer framework removed regulatory uncertainty that had held back stablecoin adoption for years, directly unlocking market growth.
insights.speaker: Chris Dixon
insights.so_what: Regulatory clarity events (like a CLARITY Act passage) can be treated as growth catalysts for the sector, not headwinds.
insights.quote: By establishing reserve requirements and a framework for issuers, it got rid of any confusion and unlocked growth.
insights.locator: The GENIUS Act showed what well-considered policymaking can achieve

insights.claim: The stablecoin market reached roughly $315 billion, up more than 50% year-over-year, since the GENIUS Act passed.
insights.speaker: Chris Dixon
insights.so_what: Quantifies the post-clarity growth rate as a benchmark for what CLARITY Act passage could do for the rest of the crypto market.
insights.quote: The stablecoin market amounts to roughly $315 billion, up more than 50% from a year ago

insights.claim: Visa's data shows stablecoins processed $100 trillion in transaction volume over the trailing twelve months, indicating stablecoin payment rails have reached massive scale.
insights.speaker: Chris Dixon
insights.so_what: A $100T annual throughput figure from a major payments network is a hard data point to track for stablecoin infrastructure adoption vs traditional rails.
insights.quote: By Visa’s count, stablecoins processed $100 trillion in transaction volume over the last twelve months.

insights.claim: Cross-border remittances via stablecoins are dramatically cheaper and faster than traditional rails: a $200 US-to-Colombia transfer costs over $12 and takes days traditionally, versus pennies and seconds via stablecoins.
insights.speaker: Chris Dixon
insights.so_what: Quantifies the cost/speed edge stablecoin rails hold over incumbent remittance corridors, a concrete wedge for stablecoin-based fintech products.
insights.quote: Sending $200 from the U.S. to Colombia via traditional rails can cost more than $12 and take days. With stablecoins, the same transfer costs pennies and settles in seconds.
insights.locator: Stablecoins are digital dollars that move across the internet

themes.theme: Stablecoins as a vehicle for dollar dominance

insights.claim: Stablecoins let people worldwide who lack traditional dollar bank access hold and transact in digital dollars through software wallets, extending U.S. dollar reach outside the traditional banking system.
insights.speaker: Chris Dixon
insights.so_what: Bullish signal for dollar-backed stablecoin issuers and U.S. monetary influence; watch for competing non-dollar stablecoin regimes as a counter-risk.
insights.quote: Millions of people worldwide who lack easy access to traditional dollar accounts can now hold and transact in digital dollars through software wallets.
insights.locator: Crucially also, the dollar is winning

themes.theme: The regulatory gap: blockchain networks remain unregulated

insights.claim: Stablecoins account for less than 15% of the crypto market by market cap, yet they depend on the remaining 85% of foundational blockchain networks that still lack a coherent federal regulatory framework.
insights.speaker: Chris Dixon
insights.so_what: Identifies where the actual regulatory risk/opportunity sits in crypto market structure — the base-layer networks, not the already-addressed stablecoin layer.
insights.quote: Stablecoins account for less than 15% of the crypto market by market cap, yet they depend on the remaining 85% of foundational blockchain networks that still operate without a coherent federal framework.

insights.claim: Dixon frames the current situation as regulating smartphones while ignoring the cellular networks they run on, arguing this is an unsustainable and incoherent regulatory posture.
insights.speaker: Chris Dixon
insights.so_what: A sticky analogy likely to recur in industry lobbying — useful shorthand for why infrastructure-layer crypto regulation is the next policy fight.
insights.quote: This is equivalent to regulating smartphones while ignoring cellular networks.

insights.claim: The CLARITY Act's core design imports proven traditional-finance safeguards — proper custody, segregation of customer assets, and full disclosure — specifically to prevent a repeat of the FTX collapse.
insights.speaker: Chris Dixon
insights.so_what: Signals the specific compliance mechanics (custody/segregation/disclosure) intermediaries and exchanges will need to meet if CLARITY passes — relevant for exchange/custody-business positioning.
insights.quote: It helps prevent the next FTX disaster by empowering regulators to supervise intermediaries with proven principles from traditional finance: proper custody, segregation of customer assets, and full disclosure.

themes.theme: Institutional infrastructure build-out is already underway

insights.claim: Major financial institutions are already building blockchain infrastructure ahead of full regulatory clarity: BlackRock has launched tokenized funds, JPMorgan is building blockchain-based payment systems, and DTCC — which holds $114 trillion in assets under custody — is preparing to scale tokenized securities via the Canton Network.
insights.speaker: Chris Dixon
insights.so_what: DTCC/Canton Network's tokenized-securities rollout is a concrete, trackable leading indicator of institutional tokenization scale; CLARITY passage could be the catalyst that lets these efforts scale further.
insights.quote: BlackRock has launched tokenized funds. JPMorgan is building blockchain-based payment systems. And DTCC, which holds $114 trillion in assets under custody, is preparing to scale tokenized securities with the Canton Network.

themes.theme: Regulatory clarity drives capital formation, not away from it

insights.claim: Crypto startup investment nearly doubled after the GENIUS Act was signed into law, rising to over $13 billion in the second half of 2025 from $6.9 billion in the pre-GENIUS first half — direct evidence that clear regulation increases rather than suppresses capital formation.
insights.speaker: Chris Dixon
insights.so_what: Empirically rebuts the 'regulation vs. innovation' tradeoff framing; a CLARITY Act passage could be read as a similar catalyst for VC deployment into blockchain-infrastructure startups.
insights.quote: During the second half of 2025 — after GENIUS was signed into law — more than $13 billion flowed into crypto startup investment, nearly double the $6.9B invested pre-GENIUS in the first half of that year.
insights.locator: Regulation versus innovation is a false choice

insights.claim: Forecasts project the tokenized asset market to grow 100x over the next few years, a scale of opportunity Dixon ties directly to whether the U.S. passes CLARITY in time to capture it domestically.
insights.speaker: Chris Dixon
insights.so_what: A headline growth figure (100x) worth tracking against actual tokenized-asset AUM over the coming years to gauge whether the forecast is playing out.
insights.quote: forecasts project the market for tokenized assets to grow 100x growth over the next few years
insights.locator: Regulation versus innovation is a false choice

themes.theme: Geopolitical framing: who writes the rules wins the infrastructure

insights.claim: Dixon frames 2026 as a repeat of the 1990s internet regulatory choice: Congress's decisions this year will determine whether the U.S. or another jurisdiction becomes the home of the next era of financial infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Chris Dixon
insights.so_what: Positions blockchain-infrastructure regulatory leadership as a competitive/geopolitical asset, not just a domestic consumer-protection issue — relevant to sovereign and cross-border capital allocation decisions.
insights.quote: The decisions Congress makes this year will determine where the next era of financial infrastructure will flourish and who writes its rules.

insights.claim: Dixon concedes the CLARITY Act is an imperfect, compromise bill that doesn't give any stakeholder everything they want, but argues it is still significantly better than the current state of no consumer protections in crypto.
insights.speaker: Chris Dixon
insights.so_what: Signals a16z's pragmatic, incrementalist lobbying posture — pushing for passage of an imperfect bill now rather than holding out for ideal legislation, useful context for handicapping CLARITY's political odds.
insights.quote: Whatever its imperfections, the CLARITY Act is significantly better than continuing with no safeguards at all.
